biography.plain_text: John Laithwaite was a British entrepreneur who founded commercial-equipment specialist JLA in West Yorkshire. Beginning with imported and second-hand laundry machines, he built a contracted rental and maintenance model serving institutions across Britain. JLA became the country's leading commercial-laundry service provider before Laithwaite sold a majority stake to private-equity firm HgCapital in 2010.

long_biography.plain_text:
A shortage of commercial dryers gave John Laithwaite his opening. While working with his father in Manchester launderettes, he imported machines from the United States and sold the surplus from home, filling his garage and borrowing space from friends. He then bought a run-down Yorkshire mill for storage and founded John Laithwaite Associates in 1973.

The young business survived an early blow when a ferry sank with a container of equipment aboard. Laithwaite responded by ordering new stock and continuing to expand. JLA moved beyond machine sales into Total Care, pairing equipment with maintenance and repair cover for a monthly payment. That recurring model attracted hospitals, care homes, hotels and residential operators, and eventually supported a private-equity transaction valuing the business at about £150 million.
